unit_name: ELEC5623 Applied Generative AI in Engineering
title: ELEC5623 Group Business Proposal (Canvas rubric)
scale_note: Points per level as in the Canvas rubric.

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: The problem is specific, meaningful and well scoped; background is supported by credible evidence; the motivation and identified gap are compelling; the need for GenAI is clearly and convincingly justified.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: The problem and motivation are clear and relevant; background is generally well supported; the role of GenAI is appropriately justified, with only minor gaps in evidence or argument.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: The problem is vague, weakly motivated or poorly supported; background is superficial; the need for GenAI is unclear or appears incidental to the proposed product.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: The criterion is not addressed, or the submitted material provides no meaningful evidence of the problem, background or motivation.

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: Target users and stakeholders are clearly identified; project scope and boundaries are precise; use cases are appropriate; functional and non-functional requirements are coherent, measurable and testable.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: Users, scope, use cases and requirements are mostly well defined; requirements are generally testable and aligned with the proposed system, with minor omissions or ambiguities.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: Requirements are incomplete, inconsistent or largely descriptive rather than testable; users, stakeholders or project scope are poorly defined.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: No meaningful requirements engineering, scope definition, stakeholder analysis or use cases are provided.

criteria.name: Proposed Product, Methodology and Technical Design

levels.label: 2 points
levels.description: The proposed solution is technically credible and clearly defined; the role of GenAI is explicit and necessary; methodology, architecture and workflow are coherent and sufficiently detailed; components and integrations form a feasible semester-scale system.

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: The technical approach is sound and mostly well explained; GenAI plays a meaningful role; architecture and workflow are appropriate, although some implementation details or technical relationships require refinement.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: A plausible technical solution is proposed, but the methodology, architecture or workflow lacks detail; the GenAI component is present but its exact role or integration is only partially explained.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: The technical design is vague, inconsistent or unrealistic; major components or workflow are missing; GenAI is used superficially or without a clear technical justification.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: No meaningful proposed methodology, architecture, workflow or technical solution is provided.

levels.label: 2 points
levels.description: The target users and value proposition are compelling; relevant alternatives or competitors are critically considered; evaluation includes clear success criteria, appropriate baselines, meaningful metrics and credible evidence collection.

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: Product value and relevant alternatives are clearly discussed; the proposed evaluation is generally appropriate and includes useful metrics and success criteria, with minor gaps.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: Basic product value and evaluation ideas are provided, but competitor/alternative analysis is limited; metrics or baselines are incomplete or only partially connected to project objectives.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: Product value is poorly justified; little meaningful analysis of alternatives is provided; evaluation relies mainly on subjective demonstrations or vague success measures.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: No meaningful product/business analysis or evaluation plan is provided.

criteria.name: Feasibility, Risk, Semester Plan and Team Roles

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: Scope is realistic and appropriately constrained; major technical and project risks are clearly identified with credible mitigation strategies; milestones are achievable and team responsibilities are clearly allocated.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: A basic semester plan and allocation of responsibilities are provided; feasibility is plausible but scope, risks or milestones require further refinement.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: The project appears overly ambitious, poorly scoped or insufficiently planned; major risks are ignored; milestones or team responsibilities are unclear.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: No meaningful evidence of feasibility analysis, risk management, semester planning or team responsibilities is provided.

levels.label: 1.5 points
levels.description: The proposal is clear, concise, coherent and professionally presented; figures and tables are effective where appropriate; external claims are supported by relevant and credible sources with consistent referencing.

levels.label: 1 points
levels.description: The proposal is understandable but contains organisational, writing or presentation issues; references are present but may be limited, inconsistently formatted or weakly connected to claims.

levels.label: 0.5 points
levels.description: The proposal is difficult to follow or poorly presented; writing contains substantial clarity issues; references are weak, inappropriate or inconsistently used.

levels.label: 0 points
levels.description: The submission lacks an acceptable professional presentation and/or provides no meaningful referencing.
